question: Should reply-session initialization conflict identity become a permanent public `error-runtime` predicate, or remain internal until OpenClaw defines a more machine-stable error contract?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but repository policy treats new Plugin SDK calls as compatibility-sensitive public API, and code review cannot choose the permanent extension contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the predicate contract
options.body: Accept the public predicate after rebasing and proving exact and wrapped conflicts preserve intended delivery behavior across representative callers.

options.title: Expose a structured error contract
options.body: Replace the message-backed public predicate with a stable exported code, discriminant, or typed outcome before migrating plugins.

options.title: Keep classification internal
options.body: Retain channel-local or injected runtime classification and avoid adding this specialized error identity to the public SDK.

recommendation.title: Approve the predicate contract
recommendation.body: Accept the public predicate after rebasing and proving exact and wrapped conflicts preserve intended delivery behavior across representative callers.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is ownership of the guarded reply-session initialization boundary and the merge of the recent conflict-semantics fix.
